Riff 0.6.32 adds composition families and reference recordings for producer reviews.

Composition families group related takes and their saved score, performance and sound material. Studio and agents can develop variations, keep their lineage and select a preferred take. Draft fields, listening controls and unfinished selections survive catalog refreshes; submissions retain pending state and show errors without losing edits.

Producer reviews can include reference recordings alongside the generated take in one audio request. Clips keep editable labels, sources and notes; review receipts record the recordings and the audio actually sent. Attributed observations and missing-reference warnings remain visible, and clips can be reused for another review. Metadata edits must finish saving before a review starts; failed saves preserve the draft and block submission.

Review forms show estimated audio and request sizes. Provider limits and errors are reported by the selected service. Reference recordings are sent to that service when a review is submitted.

Managed engine preparation uses a configured compile queue and retains build receipts and staged artifacts. If queue policy requires it, an unavailable queue stops preparation instead of starting a direct build.

Updates keep the library, recordings, saved material and settings in the persistent workspace. Verified model downloads are reused; source installations may rebuild a changed engine. Music, writing, reviews and exports must finish or be cancelled before activation.
